nodes.name: Linear-rate distributed method of Nedic et al.
nodes.statement: More recently, in \cite{ned17} new methods were proposed where it was shown that $O((m^2 + \sqrt{L/\mu}m)\log \varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations are required to find an $\varepsilon$ solution to the optimization problem when the function is $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth, where $m$ is the number of nodes in the fixed undirected network.
nodes.statement_short: Distributed method needing $O((m^2+\sqrt{L/\mu}m)\log\varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations for strongly convex smooth problems.
conclusions: $O((m^2 + \sqrt{L/\mu}m)\log \varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations are required to find an $\varepsilon$ solution to the optimization problem

nodes.name: Rate of the unifying method of Jakovetic
nodes.statement: This newly proposed general method is able to recover existing rates and achieves an $\varepsilon$ precision in $O(\sqrt{L/ (\mu \lambda_2)} \log \varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations, where $\lambda_2$ is the second largest eigenvalue of the interaction matrix.
conclusions: achieves an $\varepsilon$ precision in $O(\sqrt{L/ (\mu \lambda_2)} \log \varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations

nodes.name: Rate of the optimal distributed algorithm of Scaman et al.
nodes.statement: This new method achieves an $\varepsilon$ precision in $O(\sqrt{L/\mu}(1 + \tau / \sqrt{\gamma}) \log \varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations for \mbox{$\mu$-strongly} convex and $L$-smooth problems, where $\tau$ is the diameter of the network and $\gamma$ is the normalized eigengap of the interaction matrix.
nodes.statement_short: Scaman et al.'s method reaches $\varepsilon$ precision in $O(\sqrt{L/\mu}(1+\tau/\sqrt{\gamma})\log\varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations.
conclusions: achieves an $\varepsilon$ precision in $O(\sqrt{L/\mu}(1 + \tau / \sqrt{\gamma}) \log \varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations

nodes.name: Distributed convex optimization problem
nodes.statement: Particularly, we consider the following optimization problem \begin{align} \min_{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n} F(\mathbf{x}) & \qquad \text{where } \qquad F(\mathbf{x})\triangleq \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}f_i(\mathbf{x}), \end{align} where each $f_i: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is a convex function. Moreover, this problem needs to be solved in a distributed manner where each function $f_i$ is known by an agent $i$ only and agents can interact with other agents over a network.
nodes.statement_short: Minimize $F=\sum_i f_i$ of convex functions where agent $i$ knows only $f_i$ and communicates over a network.

nodes.name: Sum-of-local-functions problem
nodes.statement: \min_{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n} F(\mathbf{x}) & \qquad \text{where } \qquad F(\mathbf{x})\triangleq \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}f_i(\mathbf{x}),
nodes.label: main_problem

nodes.name: Matrix entry and identity notation
nodes.statement: We denote as $[A]_{ij}$ the entry of the matrix $A$ at its $i$-th row and $j$-th column and $I_{n}$ is the identity matrix of size $n$.

nodes.name: Largest singular value $\sigma_{\max}(A)$
nodes.statement: We denote the largest singular value of a matrix $A$ as $\sigma_{\max}(A) = \lambda_{\max}(A^TA) = \max \{\lambda \mid \exists x \neq 0, A^TAx = \lambda x \}$.

nodes.name: Smallest nonzero singular value $\sigma_{\min}(A)$
nodes.statement: We use $\sigma_{\min}(A) = \min \{\lambda >0 \mid \exists x \neq 0, A^TAx = \lambda x \}$ {as the smallest nonzero singular value}.

nodes.name: Condition number $\chi(A^TA)$
nodes.statement: Also, we define $\chi(A^TA) = \frac{\sigma_{\max}{(A)}}{\sigma_{\min}{(A)}}$.

nodes.name: Soft-O notation $\tilde{O}$
nodes.statement: The notation $\tilde{O}$ is used to ignore logarithmic factors in an estimate.

nodes.name: Stacked column vector
nodes.statement: Initially, let us introduce a stacked column vector ${{{x} = [x_1^T,x_2^T,\hdots,x_m^T]^T \in \mathbb{R}^{mn}}}$ to rewrite the problem in Eq. \eqref{main_problem} in an equivalent form as \begin{align*} \min_{x_1 = \hdots =x_m} {F(x)} & = \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Stack local copies $x_i$ into $x\in\mathbb{R}^{mn}$ and rewrite the problem with consensus constraint $x_1=\dots=x_m$.

nodes.name: Communication graph $\mathcal{G}$
nodes.statement: We model such a network as a fixed connected undirected graph $\mathcal{G} = (V,E)$, where $V$ is a set of {$m$} nodes and $E$ is a set of edges.

nodes.name: Network information constraints
nodes.statement: The network structure imposes information constraints, namely, each node $i$ has access to the function $f_i$ only, {and a node can exchange information only with its immediate neighbors, i.e., a node $i$ can communicate with node $j$ if and only if $(i,j)\in E$}.
nodes.statement_short: Each node knows only its own $f_i$ and communicates only with its immediate neighbours.

nodes.name: Laplacian matrix of the graph
nodes.statement: Initially, define the Laplacian matrix $\bar W{\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times m}}$ of the graph $\mathcal{G}$ as \begin{align*} [\bar W]_{ij} = \begin{cases} -1, & \text{if } (i,j) \in E,\\ \text{deg}(i), &\text{if } i= j, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise }. \end{cases} \end{align*} where $\text{deg}(i)$ is the degree of the node $i$, i.e., the number of neighbors of the node.

nodes.name: Communication (interaction) matrix
nodes.statement: Finally, define the communication matrix, sometimes called interaction matrix as $W = \bar W \otimes I_n$, where $\otimes$ indicates the Kronecker product.
nodes.statement_short: Interaction matrix $W=\bar W\otimes I_n$.

nodes.name: Properties of the interaction matrix
nodes.statement: One can verify that $W$ is a nonnegative semidefinite matrix, with the following properties: \begin{itemize} \item $W{x} = 0$ if and only if {$x_1 = \hdots = x_m$}. \item $\sqrt{W}{x} = 0$ if and only if {$x_1 = \hdots = x_m$}. \item $\sigma_{\max} (\sqrt{W}) = \lambda_{\max} (W)$. \end{itemize}
conclusions: $W$ is a nonnegative semidefinite matrix
$W{x} = 0$ if and only if {$x_1 = \hdots = x_m$}
$\sqrt{W}{x} = 0$ if and only if {$x_1 = \hdots = x_m$}
$\sigma_{\max} (\sqrt{W}) = \lambda_{\max} (W)$
nodes.statement_short: $W$ is PSD, its kernel (and that of $\sqrt W$) is the consensus subspace, and $\sigma_{\max}(\sqrt W)=\lambda_{\max}(W)$.

nodes.name: Distributed optimization with network constraint $\sqrt{W}x=0$
nodes.statement: Therefore, one can equivalently rewrite the problem in Eq. \eqref{main_problem} as: \begin{align} \min_{\sqrt{W} x=0} {F(x)} & = \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i), \end{align} where the constraint $\sqrt{W} x=0$ is equivalent to \mbox{$x_1 = \hdots = x_m$} given that $\ker (\sqrt{W}) = \mathrm{span}(\boldsymbol{1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Reformulate as minimizing $\sum_i f_i(x_i)$ subject to $\sqrt{W}x=0$.

nodes.name: Consensus-constrained problem
nodes.statement: \min_{\sqrt{W} x=0} {F(x)} & = \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i),
nodes.label: consensus_problem2

nodes.name: Euclidean setup
nodes.statement: For simplicity of exposition, we will present our results considering the $2$-norm only, which is called the Euclidean setup. Nevertheless, in Section \ref{sec:discussion} we will point out the generalization to other norms.

nodes.name: $\mu$-strongly convex function
nodes.statement: A function $f(\cdot)$ is a $\mu$-strongly convex function if for any $x,y$ it holds that \begin{align*} f(y) \geq f(x) + \left\langle \nabla f(x),y-x \right\rangle + \frac{\mu}{2}\|x-y\|^2_2, \end{align*} where $\nabla f(x)$ is any subgradient of $f(\cdot)$ at $x$.
differentia: for any $x,y$ it holds that \begin{align*} f(y) \geq f(x) + \left\langle \nabla f(x),y-x \right\rangle + \frac{\mu}{2}\|x-y\|^2_2, \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:strong

nodes.name: Strong convexity of the sum
nodes.statement: Particularly, if each of the functions $f_i(x_i)$ in the problem in Eq.\eqref{consensus_problem2} is $\mu_i$-strongly convex then $F(x)$ is $\mu$-strongly convex, with $\mu = \min\limits_{i=1,\hdots,m} \mu_i$.
assumptions: each of the functions $f_i(x_i)$ in the problem in Eq.\eqref{consensus_problem2} is $\mu_i$-strongly convex
conclusions: $F(x)$ is $\mu$-strongly convex, with $\mu = \min\limits_{i=1,\hdots,m} \mu_i$

nodes.name: $L$-smooth function ($L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient)
nodes.statement: A function $f( \cdot )$ has $L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient if it is differentiable and its gradient satisfies the Lipschitz condition, i.e. for any $x,y$ \begin{align*} \|\nabla f(x) - \nabla f(y)\|_2 & \leq L \|x-y\|_2 \end{align*} A function having $L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient is also referred as $L$-smooth.
differentia: it is differentiable and its gradient satisfies the Lipschitz condition
nodes.label: def:smooth

nodes.name: Smoothness of the sum
nodes.statement: If each of the functions $f_i(x_i)$ in the problem in Eq.\eqref{consensus_problem2} has $L_i$-Lipschitz continuous gradients then $F(x)$ has $L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient with $L = \max\limits_{i=1,\hdots,m} L_i$.
assumptions: each of the functions $f_i(x_i)$ in the problem in Eq.\eqref{consensus_problem2} has $L_i$-Lipschitz continuous gradients
conclusions: $F(x)$ has $L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient with $L = \max\limits_{i=1,\hdots,m} L_i$

nodes.name: Nesterov's Fast Gradient Method
nodes.statement: \caption{Nesterov's Fast Gradient Method} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \STATE{Choose $y_0 = x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$} \WHILE{ stopping criteria } \STATE{$x_{k+1} = y_k - \frac{1}{L} \nabla f (y_k)$} \STATE{$y_{k+1} = x_{k+1} + \frac{\sqrt{L \vphantom{\mu}} - \sqrt{\vphantom{L}\mu}}{\sqrt{L}+ \sqrt{\vphantom{L}\mu}}(x_{k+1} - x_k)$} \ENDWHILE \RETURN $x_k$ \end{algorithmic}
nodes.statement_short: Accelerated gradient descent: gradient step from $y_k$ then momentum extrapolation with coefficient $(\sqrt L-\sqrt\mu)/(\sqrt L+\sqrt\mu)$.
nodes.label: alg:nesterov

nodes.name: Convergence rate of Nesterov's Fast Gradient Method
nodes.statement: Specifically it holds for \cref{alg:nesterov} that \begin{align*} f(x_k) - f^* \leq L\left( 1- \sqrt{\frac{\mu}{L}} \right)^k\|x_0 - x^*\|_2^2, \end{align*} where $f^*$ denotes the minimum value of the function $f(x)$ and $x^*$ is its minimizer. This result implies a geometric convergence rate, where one can find a solution that is $\varepsilon$ close to the optimal in \begin{align} N = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu}} \log \left( \frac{L\|x_0 -x^*\|^2_2}{\varepsilon} \right) \right) \end{align} iterations.
nodes.statement_short: FGM converges geometrically, reaching $\varepsilon$ accuracy in $O(\sqrt{L/\mu}\log(L\|x_0-x^*\|^2/\varepsilon))$ iterations.
conclusions: f(x_k) - f^* \leq L\left( 1- \sqrt{\frac{\mu}{L}} \right)^k\|x_0 - x^*\|_2^2,
one can find a solution that is $\varepsilon$ close to the optimal in

nodes.name: FGM iteration complexity
nodes.statement: N = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu}} \log \left( \frac{L\|x_0 -x^*\|^2_2}{\varepsilon} \right) \right)
nodes.label: rate_nest

nodes.name: Linearly constrained convex problem and its Lagrangian dual
nodes.statement: In what follows we will consider a $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth function $f(x)$ and the general optimization problem with linear constraints \begin{align} \min_{Ax=0} f(x) \end{align} where the Lagrangian dual problem of Eq. \eqref{main2} is \begin{align*} \max_y \left\lbrace \min_{{x}} \left( f(x) - \left\langle A^Ty,x \right\rangle \right) \right\rbrace. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Minimize strongly convex smooth $f$ subject to $Ax=0$; Lagrangian dual is a max-min problem.

nodes.name: Linearly constrained problem
nodes.statement: \min_{Ax=0} f(x)
nodes.label: main2

nodes.name: Dual function $\varphi$ and its constants $\mu_\varphi$, $L_\varphi$
nodes.statement: Now, rewrite the Lagrangian dual problem in its equivalent form as a minimization problem \begin{align} \min_y \varphi(y) & \qquad \text{where} \qquad \varphi(y) = \max_x \left\lbrace \left\langle A^Ty,x \right\rangle -f(x) \right\rbrace, \end{align} and $\varphi(y)$ is $\mu_\varphi = \frac{\sigma_{\min}(A)}{L}$-strongly convex in $\ker(A^T)^{\perp}$ and has $L_\varphi = \frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)}{\mu}$-Lipschitz continuous gradients.
nodes.statement_short: Dual as minimization of $\varphi(y)=\max_x\{\langle A^Ty,x\rangle-f(x)\}$, $\sigma_{\min}(A)/L$-strongly convex on $\ker(A^T)^\perp$ and $\sigma_{\max}(A)/\mu$-smooth.

nodes.name: Dual problem
nodes.statement: \min_y \varphi(y) & \qquad \text{where} \qquad \varphi(y) = \max_x \left\lbrace \left\langle A^Ty,x \right\rangle -f(x) \right\rbrace,
nodes.label: dual_problem22

nodes.name: Demyanov-Danskin's theorem
nodes.statement: From the Demyanov-Danskin's theorem (see Proposition $4.5.1$ in \cite{Bertsekas2003}) it follows that \mbox{$\nabla \varphi(y) = Ax^*(A^Ty) $} where $x^*(A^Ty)$ is the unique solution to the inner maximization problem \begin{align*} x^*(A^Ty) & = arg\,max_x \left\lbrace \left\langle A^Ty,x \right\rangle -f(x) \right\rbrace. \end{align*}
conclusions: \mbox{$\nabla \varphi(y) = Ax^*(A^Ty) $}
nodes.statement_short: Gradient of the dual function is $Ax^*(A^Ty)$, with $x^*(A^Ty)$ the inner maximizer.

nodes.name: Explicit access to the dual subproblem solution
nodes.statement: Nonetheless, initially we will assume that we have access to $x^*(A^Ty)$ explicitly.

nodes.name: Dual-friendly function
nodes.statement: A function $f(x)$ is \textit{dual-friendly} if when considering the optimization problem in Eq.\eqref{main2} one has immediate access to an explicit solution $x^*(A^Ty)$ to the dual subproblem or it can be computed efficiently.
differentia: one has immediate access to an explicit solution $x^*(A^Ty)$ to the dual subproblem or it can be computed efficiently

nodes.name: Minimum-norm dual solution $y^*$
nodes.statement: If the solution is not unique, we will choose $y^*$ with the smallest norm solution.

nodes.name: Dual solution norm $R$
nodes.statement: Moreover, we will denote its norm as $R = \|y^*\|_2$ and assume that $R < \infty$.

nodes.name: Strong convexity of the dual on the space of gradients
nodes.statement: Note that we will use the result in Eq.\cref{rate_nest} applied to the dual problem in Eq.\eqref{main2}, which is not strongly convex in the ordinary sense (in the whole space). Nevertheless, since we will select $y_0 = x_0$ in \cref{alg:nesterov} as the initial condition, we will work in the linear space of gradients on which we have strong convexity.
nodes.statement_short: The dual is not strongly convex globally, but iterates stay in the gradient subspace where it is.

nodes.name: $(\varepsilon,\tilde{\varepsilon})$-optimal solution
nodes.statement: We say that a point $\hat x$ is an $(\varepsilon,\tilde{\varepsilon})$-optimal solution for the problem in Eq.\eqref{main2} if the following condition holds \begin{align*} f(\hat x ) - f(x^*) \le \varepsilon \qquad \text{and} \qquad \|A\hat x\|_2 \leq \tilde{\varepsilon}. \end{align*} where $f(x^*)$ denotes the optimal function value the problem in Eq.\eqref{main2}. Moreover note that $\left| f(x^*(A^Ty) ) - f(x^*) \right| \le \|y\|_2\|Ax^*(A^Ty)\|_2 $
nodes.statement_short: A point with primal suboptimality at most $\varepsilon$ and constraint violation $\|A\hat x\|\le\tilde\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Nesterov's Fast Gradient Method on the Dual Problem
nodes.statement: \caption{Nesterov's Fast Gradient Method on the Dual Problem} \begin{algorithmic}[1] \STATE{Choose $y_0 = \tilde{y}_0 =0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$} \WHILE{ $\|y_k\|_2 \|Ax^*(A^Ty_k)\|_2 \geq \varepsilon \text{ and } \|Ax^*(A^Ty_k)\|_2 \geq \tilde{\varepsilon}$ } \STATE{$y_{k+1} = \tilde{y}_k - \frac{1}{L_\varphi} Ax^*(A^T\tilde{y}_k)$} \STATE{$\tilde{y}_{k+1} = y_{k+1} + \frac{\sqrt{L_\varphi} - \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}} }{\sqrt{L_\varphi}+ \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}}}(y_{k+1} - y_k)$} \ENDWHILE \RETURN $y_k$ \end{algorithmic}
nodes.statement_short: FGM applied to the dual $\varphi$, using gradient $Ax^*(A^T\tilde y_k)$, stopping once primal suboptimality and infeasibility certificates fall below thresholds.
nodes.label: alg:nesterov2

nodes.name: Oracle complexity of FGM on the dual
nodes.statement: From \cite{dev12}, we can immediately conclude that the number of oracle calls (calculations of $Ax$ and $A^Ty$) required for the \cref{alg:nesterov2} is \begin{align} N & = O \left( \sqrt{\frac{L_\varphi}{\mu_\varphi}} \log \left(\max\left\lbrace 4 L_\varphi\frac{R^2}{\varepsilon} ,2 L_\varphi \frac{R}{\tilde{\varepsilon}}\right\rbrace \right) \right) = \tilde{O}\left( \sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu} \chi(A^TA) }\right). \end{align}
conclusions: the number of oracle calls (calculations of $Ax$ and $A^Ty$) required for the \cref{alg:nesterov2} is
nodes.statement_short: Algorithm 2 needs $\tilde O(\sqrt{(L/\mu)\chi(A^TA)})$ oracle calls.

nodes.name: Dual FGM oracle complexity
nodes.statement: N & = O \left( \sqrt{\frac{L_\varphi}{\mu_\varphi}} \log \left(\max\left\lbrace 4 L_\varphi\frac{R^2}{\varepsilon} ,2 L_\varphi \frac{R}{\tilde{\varepsilon}}\right\rbrace \right) \right) = \tilde{O}\left( \sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu} \chi(A^TA) }\right).
nodes.label: bound_dual

nodes.name: Distributed dual FGM (per-agent iterations)
nodes.statement: If we change of variables $\sqrt{W}y_k = z_k$ and \mbox{$\sqrt{W}\tilde y_k = \tilde z_k$}, then the resulting iterations can be executed in a distributed manner. The main observation is the interaction between agents is dictated by the term $Wx^*(\tilde z_k)$ which depends only on local information. Particularly, each node in the graph has its local variables $z_k^i$ and $\tilde z_k^i$, and to compute the value of these variables on the next iteration it only requires the information sent by the neighbors defined by the communication graph $\mathcal{G}$. Each node $i$ updates its local variables as \begin{subequations} \begin{align} z_{k+1}^i &= \tilde z_k^i - \frac{1}{L_\varphi} \sum_{j=1}^{m} W_{ij} x^{*}_j(\tilde z_k^j) \\ \tilde z_{k+1}^i &= z_{k+1}^i + \frac{\sqrt{L_\varphi} - \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}}}{\sqrt{L_\varphi}+ \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}}}(z_{k+1}^i - z_k^i) \end{align} \end{subequations} where $W_{ij} = [\bar W]_{ij} \otimes I_n$ and $x^{*}_j(w_k)$ is the components of solution of the dual subproblem shared by agent $j$.
nodes.statement_short: Run Algorithm 2 with $A=\sqrt W$ after substituting $z_k=\sqrt W y_k$, so each agent updates $z^i,\tilde z^i$ using only neighbours' dual subproblem solutions.
input: each node in the graph has its local variables $z_k^i$ and $\tilde z_k^i$

nodes.name: Per-agent update of $z^i$
nodes.statement: z_{k+1}^i &= \tilde z_k^i - \frac{1}{L_\varphi} \sum_{j=1}^{m} W_{ij} x^{*}_j(\tilde z_k^j)

nodes.name: Per-agent momentum update of $\tilde z^i$
nodes.statement: \tilde z_{k+1}^i &= z_{k+1}^i + \frac{\sqrt{L_\varphi} - \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}}}{\sqrt{L_\varphi}+ \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}}}(z_{k+1}^i - z_k^i)

nodes.name: Case 1: strongly convex and smooth
nodes.statement: Assume $F(x)$ is dual-friendly, \mbox{$L$-smooth} and $\mu$-strongly convex. Moreover, set $\tilde{\varepsilon} = \varepsilon/ R$. Then, after \begin{align*} N = O\left( \sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu}\chi(W)} \log \left( \frac{\sigma_{\max}(W)R^2}{\mu \epsilon} \right) \right) \end{align*} iterations (oracle calls) of Eqs.\cref{per_agent}, the point $x^*(z_N)$ is an $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon/R )$-optimal solution to the optimization problem in Eq.~\eqref{consensus_problem2}.
conclusions: the point $x^*(z_N)$ is an $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon/R )$-optimal solution to the optimization problem in Eq.~\eqref{consensus_problem2}
nodes.statement_short: For dual-friendly $L$-smooth $\mu$-strongly convex $F$, $O(\sqrt{(L/\mu)\chi(W)}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ distributed iterations suffice.
nodes.label: thm:case1

nodes.name: Proof of Case 1
nodes.statement: The desired result follows from the estimate in Eq.\cref{bound_dual}, the definition of $\chi(A^TA)$ and $A = \sqrt{W}$ and $\tilde \varepsilon =\varepsilon/R$.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize the dual FGM bound (6) to $A=\sqrt W$ and $\tilde\varepsilon=\varepsilon/R$.

nodes.name: Strongly convex regularized function
nodes.statement: For a convex function $f(x)$, we define the strongly convex regularized function $f^\mu(x)$ with regularizer $r^2(x)$ as \begin{align} f^\mu(x) \triangleq f(x) + \frac{\mu}{2}r^2(x). \end{align}

nodes.name: Regularized function
nodes.statement: f^\mu(x) \triangleq f(x) + \frac{\mu}{2}r^2(x).
nodes.label: regularizer

nodes.name: Case 2: strongly convex and Lipschitz
nodes.statement: Assume $F(x)$ is dual-friendly, \mbox{$M$-Lipschitz} and $\mu$-strongly convex. Then, after \begin{align*} N = \tilde O\left( \sqrt{\frac{ M^2}{\mu\varepsilon} \chi(W)} \right) \end{align*} iterations (oracle calls) of Eqs.\cref{per_agent} on the regularized dual problem $\varphi^{\mu_\varphi}(y)$, with $\mu_\varphi = \varepsilon / R^2$ and regularizer $\|y\|_2^2$, the point $x^*(z_N)$ is an $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon/R )$-optimal solution to the optimization problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus_problem2}.
conclusions: the point $x^*(z_N)$ is an $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon/R )$-optimal solution to the optimization problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus_problem2}
nodes.statement_short: For dual-friendly $M$-Lipschitz $\mu$-strongly convex $F$, $\tilde O(\sqrt{M^2\chi(W)/(\mu\varepsilon)})$ iterations on the regularized dual suffice.
nodes.label: thm:case2

nodes.name: Proof of Case 2
nodes.statement: Initially, lets construct a regularized dual problem. Then, we have that \begin{align} \min_y \varphi^{\hat\mu}(y) & = \varphi(y) + \frac{\hat\mu}{2}\|y\|_2^2 \end{align} where $\hat\mu = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2}$. Assume there exists $y_N$ such that \begin{align*} \varphi^{\hat\mu}(y_N) - \varphi^{\hat\mu}_* &\leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2} \end{align*} where $\varphi^{\hat\mu}_*$ is the optimal value of the regularized dual function. Then \begin{align*} \varphi(y_N) - \varphi^* &\leq \varepsilon. \end{align*} where $\varphi^*$ is the optimal value of the dual function. It follows from \cite{gas16b} that the number of oracle calls required to find a $(\varepsilon,\tilde{\varepsilon})$-optimal solution is \begin{align*} O\left( \sqrt{\frac{2L_\varphi(\varepsilon + 2R \tilde{\varepsilon})}{\tilde{\varepsilon}^2}}\log\left(\frac{4L_\varphi \left( \min\limits_{Ax=0}F(x)-\min\limits_x F(x))(\varepsilon+2R\tilde{\varepsilon}\right) }{\varepsilon\cdot \tilde{\varepsilon}^2}\right)\right) \end{align*} Additionally, from Theorem $3$ in \cite{lan17} it follows that \begin{align} R^2 & = \|y^*\|_2^2 \leq \frac{\|\nabla F(x^*)\|_2^2}{\sigma_{\min}(A)} = \frac{M^2}{\sigma_{\min}(A)}. \end{align} The final results follow by the definitions of $\tilde\varepsilon$ and $L_\varphi$.
nodes.statement_short: Regularize the dual with $\hat\mu=\varepsilon/R^2$, apply the known FGM complexity for $(\varepsilon,\tilde\varepsilon)$-optimality, and bound $R^2\le M^2/\sigma_{\min}(A)$.

nodes.name: Regularized dual problem
nodes.statement: \min_y \varphi^{\hat\mu}(y) & = \varphi(y) + \frac{\hat\mu}{2}\|y\|_2^2
nodes.label: dual_regularized

nodes.name: Bound on the dual solution norm
nodes.statement: R^2 & = \|y^*\|_2^2 \leq \frac{\|\nabla F(x^*)\|_2^2}{\sigma_{\min}(A)} = \frac{M^2}{\sigma_{\min}(A)}.
nodes.label: Soomin_bound

nodes.name: Unknown $R$ and restarting
nodes.statement: Note that we typically do not know $R^2 = \|y^*\|_2^2$. Thus, we require a method to estimate the strong convexity parameter $\hat{\mu}$ which is challenging \cite{nes07,odo15}. Therefore, we can apply the restarting technique on $\mu$ \cite{odo15}. The payment for that is just an $8$ multiplicative factor in the estimation \cite{iou14}. Similarly, a generalization of the FGM algorithm can be proposed when $L_\varphi$ is unknown \cite{ani17}. The specific details of this generalizations are out of the scope of this paper.
nodes.statement_short: Since $R$ is unknown, restart on $\mu$ at an 8x cost; unknown $L_\varphi$ handled by a generalized FGM.

nodes.name: Case 3: smooth convex
nodes.statement: Assume $F(x)$ is dual-friendly and $L$-smooth convex. Then, after \begin{align*} N =\tilde O\left( \sqrt{\frac{ LR_x^2}{\varepsilon} \chi(W)} \right) \end{align*} iterations (oracle calls) of Eqs.\cref{per_agent} on the dual problem of the regularized function $F^\mu(x)$ with $\mu = \varepsilon / R_x^2 = \varepsilon / \|x^* - x^*(z_0)\|_2^2$ and regularizer $\|x - x^*(z_0)\|_2^2$, the point $x^*(z_N)$ is an \mbox{$(\varepsilon,\varepsilon/R )$-optimal} solution to the optimization problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus_problem2}.
conclusions: the point $x^*(z_N)$ is an \mbox{$(\varepsilon,\varepsilon/R )$-optimal} solution to the optimization problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus_problem2}
nodes.statement_short: For dual-friendly $L$-smooth convex $F$, $\tilde O(\sqrt{LR_x^2\chi(W)/\varepsilon})$ iterations on the dual of the primal-regularized problem suffice.
nodes.label: thm:case3

nodes.name: Proof of Case 3
nodes.statement: We can regularize the primal problem in Eq. \eqref{main2} such that we instead try to solve \begin{align*} \min_{Ax=0} F(x) + \frac{\mu}{2}\|x -x^*(z_0)\|_2^2, \end{align*} with $\mu = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2_x}$. Additionally, if the minimizer $x^*$ is not unique we will consider it as the closest solution from $x^*(z_0)$, i.e. closest to the initial point of the algorithm. This take us back to the case of \cref{sec:strong_smooth} for which we can conclude that up to logarithmic factor that the number of iterations required is: \begin{align} \tilde{O}\left( \sqrt{\frac{L R_x^2}{\varepsilon}\chi(A^TA)}\right). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Regularize the primal with $\mu=\varepsilon/R_x^2$ to reduce to Case 1.

nodes.name: Iteration bound for smooth case
nodes.statement: \tilde{O}\left( \sqrt{\frac{L R_x^2}{\varepsilon}\chi(A^TA)}\right).
nodes.label: result_smooth

nodes.name: Case 4: Lipschitz convex
nodes.statement: Assume $F(x)$ is dual-friendly and $M$-Lipschitz. Then, after \begin{align*} N = \tilde O\left( \sqrt{\frac{ M^2R_x^2}{\varepsilon^2} \chi(W)} \right) \end{align*} iterations (oracle calls) of Eqs.\cref{per_agent} on the regularized dual problem $\varphi^{\mu_\varphi}(y)$, with $\mu_\varphi = \varepsilon / R^2$ and regularizer $\|y\|_2^2$, of the regularized function $F^\mu(x)$ with $\mu = \varepsilon / R_x^2$ and regularizer $\|x - x^*(z_0)\|_2^2$, the point $x^*(z_N)$ is an \mbox{$(\varepsilon,\varepsilon/R )$-optimal} solution to the optimization problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus_problem2}.
conclusions: the point $x^*(z_N)$ is an \mbox{$(\varepsilon,\varepsilon/R )$-optimal} solution to the optimization problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus_problem2}
nodes.statement_short: For dual-friendly $M$-Lipschitz $F$, $\tilde O(\sqrt{M^2R_x^2\chi(W)/\varepsilon^2})$ iterations with primal and dual regularization suffice.
nodes.label: thm:case4

nodes.name: Proof of Case 4
nodes.statement: Similarly as in the cases above we will use regularization. We will regularize the primal problem with $\mu = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2_x}$ and then regularize the dual problem too with $\hat{\mu} = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2}$. Therefore, up to logarithmic factors the \cref{alg:nesterov2} will stop in no more than \begin{align} O\left( \sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)R^2_x(\varepsilon+2R\tilde{\varepsilon})}{\varepsilon\tilde\varepsilon^2}}\right) \end{align} iterations. Where the estimate in Eq. \eqref{result2_convex} is unimporvable up to logarithmic factors.
nodes.statement_short: Double regularization: primal with $\varepsilon/R_x^2$ and dual with $\varepsilon/R^2$, then bound Algorithm 2's stopping time.

nodes.name: Iteration bound for Lipschitz case
nodes.statement: O\left( \sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)R^2_x(\varepsilon+2R\tilde{\varepsilon})}{\varepsilon\tilde\varepsilon^2}}\right)
nodes.label: result2_convex

nodes.name: Weights with $\chi(W)=O(m^2)$ on fixed undirected graphs
nodes.statement: Particularly, for fixed undirected graphs, one can construct a set of weights $W$ for which $\chi(W) = O(m^2)$ \cite{ols14}.
conclusions: one can construct a set of weights $W$ for which $\chi(W) = O(m^2)$

nodes.name: Prefer the constraint $\sqrt{W}x=0$ over $Wx=0$
nodes.statement: As an immediate conclusion it is clear that the form in Eq.\eqref{consensus_problem2} with the constraint described as \mbox{$\sqrt{W}x=0$} should be preferred over the description as $Wx=0$, even though both representation correctly describe the consensus subspace $x_1 = \hdots x_m$. Particularly, when we pick $A = \sqrt{W}$, we have \mbox{$\chi(A^TA) = \chi(W)$} instead of \mbox{$\chi(W^TW) = \chi(W^2) \gg \chi(W)$}.
nodes.statement_short: Using $A=\sqrt W$ gives condition number $\chi(W)$ rather than $\chi(W^2)$.

nodes.name: Values of $\chi(W)$ for standard graphs
nodes.statement: For example for a star graph \mbox{$\sqrt{\chi(W)} = O( \sqrt{m})$}, for complete graphs $\sqrt{\chi(W)} = O(1)$, for path graphs \mbox{$\sqrt{\chi(W)} \sim \text{diam}(\mathcal{G}) = O( m)$}, for regular networks $\sqrt{\chi(W)} \geq \frac{\text{diam}(G)}{\log m}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\sqrt{\chi(W)}$ is $O(\sqrt m)$ for stars, $O(1)$ for complete graphs, $O(m)$ for paths.

nodes.name: Average consensus problem
nodes.statement: Assume that each node in the graph $\mathcal{G}$ holds an initial numeric value {$x^i_0$} and can compute the {weighted} average of the values {held} by its neighbors at each iteration. {Let $x^i_k$ be the value of node $i$ at iteration $k$.} {We would like to know} how many iterations are required (and what is the proper algorithm) to reach consensus.
nodes.statement_short: Nodes holding values and averaging neighbours: how many iterations (and which algorithm) reach consensus?

nodes.name: $\varepsilon$-consensus
nodes.statement: Particularly, we will reach $\varepsilon$-consensus if for any $\varepsilon > 0$ \begin{align*} \sqrt{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{{m}} \left(x^i_N - \frac{1}{{m}} \sum\limits_{j=1}^{{m}}{x^j_0}\right)^2} & \leq \varepsilon \sqrt{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{{m}} \left({x^i_0} - \frac{1}{{m}} \sum\limits_{j=1}^{{m}}{x^j_0}\right)^2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Distance to the initial average shrinks by factor $\varepsilon$ relative to initial spread.

nodes.name: Consensus as a quadratic minimization
nodes.statement: This problem can be solved by considering the convex optimization problem \begin{align} \min_{{x}} \frac{1}{2} \left\langle {x,Wx} \right\rangle. \end{align} where $W$ is a communication matrix as defined in Section \ref{sec:problem}.

nodes.name: Consensus quadratic problem
nodes.statement: \min_{{x}} \frac{1}{2} \left\langle {x,Wx} \right\rangle.
nodes.label: consensus

nodes.name: Iteration complexity of accelerated consensus
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:case1} provides a direct estimate on the number of iterations required to reach consensus, particularly we need $O(\sqrt{\chi(W)}\log \varepsilon^{-1})$, where we have used the fact that \cref{consensus} is $\sigma_{\min}(\sqrt{W})$-strongly convex in $x_0 +\ker(W)$ and has $\sigma_{\max}(\sqrt{W})$-Lipschitz continuous gradients.
assumptions: \cref{consensus} is $\sigma_{\min}(\sqrt{W})$-strongly convex in $x_0 +\ker(W)$ and has $\sigma_{\max}(\sqrt{W})$-Lipschitz continuous gradients
conclusions: we need $O(\sqrt{\chi(W)}\log \varepsilon^{-1})$
nodes.statement_short: Consensus is reached in $O(\sqrt{\chi(W)}\log\varepsilon^{-1})$ iterations by Case 1.

nodes.name: Optimality of the consensus estimate
nodes.statement: Moreover, it follows that this estimate cannot be improved up to constant factors.
conclusions: this estimate cannot be improved up to constant factors

nodes.name: FGM respects the network information constraints
nodes.statement: It is important to remark that the Fast Gradient Method, with $x^i_0 = \tilde y^i_0$, {does respect the information constraints imposed by the network}. That is, each node only requires the computation of the average of its immediate neighbors and aggregation can be performed in a fully distributed manner.

nodes.name: Optimality of the four case estimates
nodes.statement: The estimates presented in the \cref{thm:case1,thm:case2,thm:case3,thm:case4} cannot be improved up to logarithmic factors.
conclusions: The estimates presented in the \cref{thm:case1,thm:case2,thm:case3,thm:case4} cannot be improved up to logarithmic factors

nodes.name: Argument for optimality of the case estimates
nodes.statement: Particularly in the smooth cases where $L < \infty$ these estimations follow (up to logarithmic factors) form the classical centralized complexity estimation of the FGM algorithm, where for a $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth convex problem we require at most \begin{align*} O\left( \sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu} }\log \left( \frac{\mu R_x^2}{\varepsilon}\right) \right) \end{align*} oracle calls and for a $L$-smooth convex problem we require at most \begin{align*} O\left( \sqrt{\frac{LR_x^2}{\varepsilon}}\right) . \end{align*} oracle calls. In addition to these centralized estimates we need to take into account the fact that one has to perform $\sqrt{\chi(W)} \log (\varepsilon^{-1})$ additional consensus steps at each iteration of the classical FGM.
nodes.statement_short: Compare with classical centralized FGM lower complexity bounds plus the unavoidable $\sqrt{\chi(W)}\log\varepsilon^{-1}$ consensus cost per iteration.

nodes.name: Power method for consensus
nodes.statement: Thus, one can apply a simple power method such as $x^{k+1} = Px^k$ to find the consensus value (see ergodic theorem for Markov Chains).
nodes.statement_short: Repeated neighbour averaging $x^{k+1}=Px^k$ with a stochastic matrix $P$.

nodes.name: Iteration complexity of the non-accelerated consensus power method
nodes.statement: As a result the number of required iterations is $O(\chi(W)\log \varepsilon^{-1})$ (\cite{ned09,tsi84,ber89}).
conclusions: the number of required iterations is $O(\chi(W)\log \varepsilon^{-1})$

nodes.name: Accelerated consensus on directed graphs
nodes.statement: However, it is still an open question whether one can get accelerated rates as those provided by \cref{alg:nesterov2} when the graph is directed.

nodes.name: Distributed computation of the dual subproblem
nodes.statement: Note that the dual subproblem can also be computed in a distributed manner. Specifically, we have that \begin{align*} arg\,max_x \left\lbrace \left\langle A^Ty,x \right\rangle -f(x) \right\rbrace & = arg\,max_{x_i, i=1,\hdots,m} \left\lbrace \left\langle \sum_{j=1}^{m} A^T_{ij }y_j,x_i \right\rangle -f_i(x_i) \right\rbrace. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
conclusions: the dual subproblem can also be computed in a distributed manner
nodes.statement_short: The dual subproblem decomposes into independent per-agent maximizations.

nodes.name: Inexact dual subproblem for smooth objectives
nodes.statement: When the function is smooth or when is strongly convex and smooth, one can solve the auxiliary problem \begin{align*} \max_x \left\lbrace \left\langle y ,Ax \right\rangle -f(x) \right\rbrace & = \left\langle y ,Ax^*(A^Ty) \right\rangle -f(x^*(A^Ty)) \end{align*} using fast gradient methods (if the function is smooth, one should make one additional regularization $\mu = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2_x}$) applied for the strongly convex problem. Therefore, we can find a solution for the dual problem, i.e. $x^*(A^Ty)$, in a logarithmic number of iterations from a desired relative precision $\delta$. This fact allows us avoid considering the error in the computation of $x^*(A^Ty)$. When the function is strongly convex and smooth, we can solve the auxiliary problem in $O\left( \sqrt{\frac{L}{\mu}} \log(\delta^{-1})\right) $ oracle calls (oracle call is the calculation of $\nabla f(x)$). On the other hand, when the function is only smooth, we require $O\left( \sqrt{ \frac{LR_x^2}{\varepsilon} }\log (\delta^{-1})\right)$ iterations. Both estimates are optimal up to logarithmic factor. Therefore, in those cases, we propose totally optimal methods.
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
nodes.statement_short: For smooth (or strongly convex smooth) $f$, solve the inner problem by FGM to precision $\delta$ at logarithmic cost, giving totally optimal methods.

nodes.name: Saddle-point form of the constrained problem
nodes.statement: \min_{Ax=0} f(x) & = \min_x \left\lbrace \max_y \left\lbrace \left\langle y,Ax \right\rangle -f(x) \right\rbrace \right\rbrace \nonumber \\ & = \max_y \left\lbrace \min_x \left\lbrace f(x) + \left\langle y,Ax \right\rangle \right\rbrace \right\rbrace

nodes.label: nes_smooth

nodes.name: Smoothed penalty $G_\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Moreover, by using the bound in Eq. \eqref{Soomin_bound}, we can replace the function \begin{align*} G(Ax) = \max_y \left\langle y,Ax\right\rangle \end{align*} by \begin{align*} G_\varepsilon(Ax) = \max_y \left\lbrace \left\langle y,Ax \right\rangle - \frac{\varepsilon}{2R^2} \|y\|_2^2\right\rbrace = \frac{R^2}{2\varepsilon} \|Ax\|_2^2. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
nodes.statement_short: Replace $G(Ax)=\max_y\langle y,Ax\rangle$ by its smoothing $G_\varepsilon(Ax)=\frac{R^2}{2\varepsilon}\|Ax\|^2$.

nodes.name: Gradient Lipschitz constant of $G_\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Finally, one can show that the function $G_\varepsilon(Ax)$ has a $\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A^T)R^2}{\varepsilon}$-Lipschitz continuous gradient, (note that $\sigma_{\max}(A^T) = \sigma_{\max}(A)$).
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
conclusions: the function $G_\varepsilon(Ax)$ has a $\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A^T)R^2}{\varepsilon}$-Lipschitz continuous gradient

nodes.name: Composite smooth/non-smooth problem
nodes.statement: So, we can solve the composite type mixed smooth/non-smooth type problem \begin{align} \min_{\|x\|_2 \leq R_x } \underbrace{G_\varepsilon(Ax)}_{\sim \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\text{-Lipschitz gradient}} + \underbrace{f(x)}_{M-\text{Lipschitz}} \end{align} where gradient oracle for $G_\varepsilon(Ax)$ requires a constant number of $Ax$ multiplications (because we can explicitly write the formula for $\nabla G_\varepsilon (z)$) and the gradient oracle for $f(x)$ requires one $\nabla f(x)$ calculations.
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
nodes.statement_short: Minimize smooth penalty $G_\varepsilon(Ax)$ plus $M$-Lipschitz $f$ over a ball.

nodes.name: Composite problem
nodes.statement: \min_{\|x\|_2 \leq R_x } \underbrace{G_\varepsilon(Ax)}_{\sim \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\text{-Lipschitz gradient}} + \underbrace{f(x)}_{M-\text{Lipschitz}}
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
nodes.label: composite

nodes.name: Complexity via Lan's accelerated gradient sliding
nodes.statement: Using Lan's accelerated gradient sliding \cite{lan16}, one can find an $\varepsilon$-solution (in function value) of Eq. \eqref{composite} without any auxiliary dual problem, after \begin{align*} N_{Ax} &= O\left( \sqrt{\frac{\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)R^2}{\varepsilon}R_x^2}{\varepsilon}} \right) = O\left( \sqrt{\frac{M^2R_x^2}{\varepsilon^2} \chi(A^TA)}\right) \end{align*} oracle calls, i.e., $Ax$ multiplications and \begin{align*} N_{\nabla f(x)} &= O\left( \frac{M^2 R_x^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right) \end{align*} oracle calls, i.e., $\nabla f(x)$-gradient calculations.
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
conclusions: one can find an $\varepsilon$-solution (in function value) of Eq. \eqref{composite} without any auxiliary dual problem
nodes.statement_short: Gradient sliding solves the composite problem with $O(\sqrt{M^2R_x^2\chi/\varepsilon^2})$ $Ax$ products and $O(M^2R_x^2/\varepsilon^2)$ gradients.

nodes.name: Restart argument for strongly convex sliding
nodes.statement: Using the restart technique \cite{iou14,jud11} one can extend Lan's accelerated gradient sliding for $f(x)$ being $\mu$-strongly convex. At the $k$-th restart the number of oracle calls is \mbox{$N_{Ax}=O\left( \sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)R^2}{\mu\varepsilon}}\right)$} computations of $Ax$ and $N_{\nabla f(x)} = O\left( \frac{2^kM^2 }{\varepsilon^2 R_x^2}\right) $ oracle calls for $\nabla f(x)$.
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
nodes.statement_short: Restart Lan's gradient sliding; per-restart costs sum geometrically.

nodes.name: Improved estimates for strongly convex composite problem
nodes.statement: This allows to improve estimates for the problem in Eq. \eqref{composite} in the following manner: \begin{align} N_{Ax} & = O\left( \sqrt{\frac{M^2}{\mu \varepsilon} \chi(A^TA)} \log \left( \frac{\mu R^2_x}{\varepsilon}\right) \right) \end{align} computations of $Ax$ and \begin{align} N_{\nabla f(x)} & = O \left( \frac{ M^2 }{\mu\varepsilon}\right) \end{align} oracle calls of $\nabla f(x)$, where these estimates are optimal up to logarithmic factors.
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
conclusions: these estimates are optimal up to logarithmic factors
nodes.statement_short: With strong convexity: $\tilde O(\sqrt{M^2\chi/(\mu\varepsilon)})$ $Ax$ products and $O(M^2/(\mu\varepsilon))$ gradients.

nodes.name: Communication complexity with restarts
nodes.statement: N_{Ax} & = O\left( \sqrt{\frac{M^2}{\mu \varepsilon} \chi(A^TA)} \log \left( \frac{\mu R^2_x}{\varepsilon}\right) \right)
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
nodes.label: prox1

nodes.name: Gradient complexity with restarts
nodes.statement: N_{\nabla f(x)} & = O \left( \frac{ M^2 }{\mu\varepsilon}\right)
nodes.section: 6 No Explicit Dual Solution is available
nodes.label: prox2

nodes.name: Proximal saddle function $G(y,z)$
nodes.statement: Let us consider the case when $f(x)$ is convex, but not strongly convex nor smooth, and return to Eq. \eqref{nes_smooth} which can be rewritten as \begin{align*} \min_{Ax=0} f(x) & = \max_y \min_x \left\lbrace f(x) + \left\langle y,Ax \right\rangle \right\rbrace \\ & = \max_y \min_z \underbrace{\min_x \left\lbrace f(x) + \left\langle y,Ax \right\rangle + \frac{1}{2} \|x-z\|_2^2 \right\rbrace }_{G(y,z)}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proximal-friendly function
nodes.statement: We will say the function $f(x)$ is \textit{proximal-friendly}, if we can solve the auxiliary strongly convex problem \begin{align*} \text{prox}_{f,A^Ty} (z) & = arg\,min_x \left\lbrace f(x) + \left\langle y,Ax \right\rangle + \frac{1}{2}\|x-z\|_2^2\right\rbrace \end{align*} explicitly, similarly as the definition of \textit{dual-friendly}.
differentia: we can solve the auxiliary strongly convex problem

nodes.name: Saddle-point complexity for smooth convex-concave problems
nodes.statement: Therefore, given that \begin{align*} \|\nabla G(y',z') - \nabla G(y,z) \|_2 & \leq L_y\|y' - y\|_2 +L_z\|z' - z\|_2 , \end{align*} one can find an $\varepsilon$- solution (in terms of the duality gap) of the saddle point problem \begin{align*} \max_{\|y\|_2\leq R} \min_z G(y,z) \end{align*} after $N_{Ax} = O\left( \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\right) $, $Ax$ multiplications, see \cite{bub15}, section $5.2$.
conclusions: one can find an $\varepsilon$- solution (in terms of the duality gap) of the saddle point problem

nodes.name: No acceleration from inexact prox
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, this does not provide any acceleration. Since, to find $\text{prox}_{f,A^Ty}(z)$ typically, one has to find an $\varepsilon$-solution of a strongly convex optimization problem. This can be done in $O(\frac{1}{\varepsilon})$ calculations of $\nabla f(x)$. So the total number of iterations will be of the order $N_{\nabla f(x)} = O\left( \frac{1}{\varepsilon^2}\right) $.
nodes.statement_short: Computing the prox inexactly costs $O(1/\varepsilon)$ gradients, so $O(1/\varepsilon^2)$ total.

nodes.name: Proximal reformulation of the dual
nodes.statement: Now, let us propose another approach, consider the original problem in Eq. \eqref{main2} and add the additional term $\frac{1}{2}\|Ax\|_2^2$ which is identically zero on any feasible point $Ax=0$. Thus, \begin{align*} \min_{Ax=0} f(x) & = \min_{Ax=0} \left\lbrace f(x) + \frac{1}{2}\|Ax\|_2^2\right\rbrace \\ & = \min_{x,z;Ax=Az} \left\lbrace f(x) + \max_y \left\langle -y,Az \right\rangle + \frac{1}{2}\|Ax\|_2^2 \right\rbrace \\ & =\min_{x,z} \left\lbrace f(x) + \max_y \left\langle -y,Az \right\rangle + \max_{y'} \left\langle y',Az-Ax \right\rangle + \frac{1}{2}\|Ax\|_2^2 \right\rbrace \\ & = - \min_{y,y'} \left\lbrace \max_x \left( \left\langle A^Ty',x \right\rangle -f(x)\right) +\max_{u \in \text{Im}A} \left\lbrace \left\langle y-y',u \right\rangle - \frac{1}{2} \|u\|^2_2 \right\rbrace \right\rbrace ^{Az=u}\\ & = - \min_{y,y'} \left\lbrace \varphi(y') + \frac{1}{2}\| \text{proj}_{\ker(A^T)^{\perp} }(y - y') \|_2^2\right\rbrace \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Add the zero term $\frac12\|Ax\|^2$ and dualize to get a proximal version of the dual problem.

nodes.name: Acceleration for proximal-friendly dual
nodes.statement: If $\varphi(y') $ is proximal friendly, we can solve the auxiliary problem (this is the proximal version of the standard dual problem) explicitly, then using accelerated proximal gradient descent (in the space of $y$) one can find an $\varepsilon$ solution to the dual problem in $ O\left( \varepsilon^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) $ proximal steps \cite{par14}.
conclusions: one can find an $\varepsilon$ solution to the dual problem in $  O\left( \varepsilon^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) $ proximal steps

nodes.name: Strong convexity and smoothness of the sum
nodes.statement: Considering the problem in Eq. \eqref{main_problem}, if each $f_i(x_i)$ is a $\mu_i$-strongly convex function , and has $L_i$-Lipschitz continuous gradients, then $F(x) $ is a \mbox{$\mu = \min_{i=1,\hdots,m}\mu_i$-strongly} convex and has $L = \max_{i=1,\hdots,m}L_i$-Lipschitz continuous gradients.
nodes.section: 8 Improving the condition number $\frac{L}{\mu}$ when $F(x)$ is strongly convex and smooth
conclusions: $F(x) $ is a \mbox{$\mu = \min_{i=1,\hdots,m}\mu_i$-strongly} convex and has $L = \max_{i=1,\hdots,m}L_i$-Lipschitz continuous gradients

nodes.name: Regularized consensus problem $F_\alpha$
nodes.statement: To overcome this drawback, we can formulate another regularization for the problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus_problem2} as \begin{align} \min_{\sqrt{W} x=0} F_\alpha (x) & = \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i) + \frac{\alpha}{2}\left\langle x,Wx\right\rangle \end{align}
nodes.section: 8 Improving the condition number $\frac{L}{\mu}$ when $F(x)$ is strongly convex and smooth

nodes.name: Regularized consensus objective
nodes.statement: \min_{\sqrt{W} x=0} F_\alpha (x) & = \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i) + \frac{\alpha}{2}\left\langle x,Wx\right\rangle
nodes.section: 8 Improving the condition number $\frac{L}{\mu}$ when $F(x)$ is strongly convex and smooth
nodes.label: better_cond

nodes.name: Condition of the regularized function $F_\alpha$
nodes.statement: Furthermore, the regularized function $F_\alpha$ is $\mu \geq \min \left\lbrace \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}\mu_i,\alpha \lambda_{\min}(W)\right\rbrace $-strongly convex and has \mbox{$L \leq \left( \max\limits_{i=1,\hdots,m}L_i + \alpha \lambda_{\max}(W)\right) $-Lipschitz} continuous gradient.
nodes.section: 8 Improving the condition number $\frac{L}{\mu}$ when $F(x)$ is strongly convex and smooth
conclusions: the regularized function $F_\alpha$ is $\mu \geq \min \left\lbrace \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}\mu_i,\alpha \lambda_{\min}(W)\right\rbrace $-strongly convex

nodes.name: Complexity with improved condition number
nodes.statement: Moreover, if we set \mbox{$\alpha \simeq \sum\limits_{k=1}^{m}\mu_k / \lambda_{\min}(W)$}, one can solve the problem in Eq. \eqref{better_cond} with relative precision $\varepsilon$ after (see also \cite{ned16w}) \begin{align*} N_{Wx} & =O\left( \left( \frac{\max\limits_{i=1,\hdots,m}L_i}{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}\mu_i} + \chi(W)\right) \sqrt{\chi(W)} \log^2(\varepsilon^{-1})\right) \end{align*} communication steps and \begin{align*} N_{\nabla F(x)} = O\left( N_{Wx} \log^{-1}(\varepsilon^{-1})\right) \end{align*} gradient $\nabla F(x)$ calculations.
nodes.section: 8 Improving the condition number $\frac{L}{\mu}$ when $F(x)$ is strongly convex and smooth
conclusions: one can solve the problem in Eq. \eqref{better_cond} with relative precision $\varepsilon$ after (see also \cite{ned16w})
nodes.statement_short: Choosing $\alpha\approx\sum\mu_k/\lambda_{\min}(W)$ replaces $\min\mu_i$ by $\sum\mu_i$ in the condition number at an additive $\chi(W)$ cost.

nodes.name: Extension of the improved-condition result to smooth functions
nodes.statement: Using the regularization technique with $\mu_i = \frac{\varepsilon}{mR^2_{x_i}} = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2_x}$ one can extend this result to the case where the function is just smooth.
nodes.section: 8 Improving the condition number $\frac{L}{\mu}$ when $F(x)$ is strongly convex and smooth
conclusions: one can extend this result to the case where the function is just smooth

nodes.name: Optimal rates on time-varying and directed graphs
nodes.statement: Nevertheless, it is an open problem to show that optimal convergence rates, comparable to those in the centralized case can be achieved for time-varying and directed graphs.

nodes.name: Gradient descent consensus on time-varying graphs
nodes.statement: One can solve the problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus} with relative precision by the simple gradient descent method on $\chi(W)\log \varepsilon^{-1}$ communication steps because this dynamic has a Lyapunov function: that is the square distance between the current point and $\ker(W)$.
conclusions: One can solve the problem in Eq. \eqref{consensus} with relative precision by the simple gradient descent method on $\chi(W)\log \varepsilon^{-1}$ communication steps

nodes.name: Accelerated consensus on time-varying graphs
nodes.statement: Whether acceleration is possible for time-varying graphs remains an open question to the best of the authors' knowledge.

nodes.name: Restarting estimate for infrequently changing graphs
nodes.statement: On the other side, if one can detect the moment the graph changes, and such changes don't happen very often one can use restarting techniques \cite{fer16,gas17}, which provide the following estimations for the number of communication steps needed \begin{align*} \sqrt{\max_W \left( \frac{ \sigma_{\max}(\sqrt{W})}{\sigma_{\min}(\sqrt{W})}\right) } \log \varepsilon^{-1}. \end{align*}
assumptions: one can detect the moment the graph changes, and such changes don't happen very often
conclusions: the following estimations for the number of communication steps needed

nodes.name: Chebyshev acceleration for fast gossip
nodes.statement: Chebyshev acceleration is suggested in \cite{sca17}, where instead of using the interaction matrix $W$ one can analyze the algorithm with a different one $P_K(W)$. $P_K(W)$ is a polynomial of degree $K$, and its eigengap is maximized with a specific choice based on Chebyshev polynomials. If $K$ is chosen as $\sqrt{\chi(W)}$ then \mbox{$\chi\left( P_{\sqrt{\chi(W)}}(W)\right) \sim 1$}.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $W$ by a Chebyshev polynomial $P_K(W)$ of degree $\sqrt{\chi(W)}$ to make its condition number $O(1)$.

nodes.name: Block $p$-norm
nodes.statement: Let's introduce a norm \mbox{$\| x\|^2_p = \|x_1\|_p^2 + ... + \|x_m\|_p^2$} for \mbox{$p\geq 1$} and assume that $F(x)$ is $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient in this (new) norm $\|\cdot \|_p$ (in $\mathbb{R}^{mn}$), see \cite{nes15}~(Lemma 1), \cite{dvu17b}~(Lemma 1) and \cite{nes05}~(Theorem 1)..

nodes.name: Condition number $\chi(W)$ for $p$-norms
nodes.statement: Thus \begin{align*} \chi(W) = \frac{\max_{\|h\|=1} \frac{<h,Wh>}{\mu}}{\min_{\|h\|=1, h \perp \text{ker}(W)} \frac{<h,Wh>}{L}} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Initialize $y_0=x_0$
nodes.statement: {Choose $y_0 = x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$}

nodes.name: Main loop
nodes.statement_short: Iterate until the stopping criterion holds.

nodes.name: Gradient step
nodes.statement: {$x_{k+1} = y_k - \frac{1}{L} \nabla f (y_k)$}
nodes.statement_short: Gradient step of length $1/L$ from $y_k$.

nodes.name: Momentum extrapolation
nodes.statement: {$y_{k+1} = x_{k+1} + \frac{\sqrt{L \vphantom{\mu}} - \sqrt{\vphantom{L}\mu}}{\sqrt{L}+ \sqrt{\vphantom{L}\mu}}(x_{k+1} - x_k)$}
nodes.statement_short: Extrapolate with momentum coefficient $(\sqrt L-\sqrt\mu)/(\sqrt L+\sqrt\mu)$.

nodes.name: Return $x_k$
nodes.statement: \RETURN $x_k$

nodes.name: Initialize dual iterates at zero
nodes.statement: {Choose $y_0 = \tilde{y}_0 =0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$}

nodes.name: Loop until approximate optimality certificate
nodes.statement_short: Loop while the duality-gap bound $\|y_k\|\|Ax^*\|$ or infeasibility $\|Ax^*\|$ is above threshold.

nodes.name: Dual gradient step
nodes.statement: {$y_{k+1} = \tilde{y}_k - \frac{1}{L_\varphi} Ax^*(A^T\tilde{y}_k)$}
nodes.statement_short: Gradient step on the dual using $\nabla\varphi=Ax^*(A^T\tilde y_k)$.

nodes.name: Dual momentum extrapolation
nodes.statement: {$\tilde{y}_{k+1} = y_{k+1} + \frac{\sqrt{L_\varphi} - \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}} }{\sqrt{L_\varphi}+ \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}}}(y_{k+1} - y_k)$}
nodes.statement_short: Momentum extrapolation with dual condition number.

nodes.name: Return $y_k$
nodes.statement: \RETURN $y_k$

nodes.name: Change of variables to $z_k$
nodes.statement: If we change of variables $\sqrt{W}y_k = z_k$ and \mbox{$\sqrt{W}\tilde y_k = \tilde z_k$}, then the resulting iterations can be executed in a distributed manner.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $z_k=\sqrt W y_k$, $\tilde z_k=\sqrt W\tilde y_k$ so iterations become local.

nodes.name: Per-agent local updates
nodes.statement: Each node $i$ updates its local variables as \begin{subequations} \begin{align} z_{k+1}^i &= \tilde z_k^i - \frac{1}{L_\varphi} \sum_{j=1}^{m} W_{ij} x^{*}_j(\tilde z_k^j) \\ \tilde z_{k+1}^i &= z_{k+1}^i + \frac{\sqrt{L_\varphi} - \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}}}{\sqrt{L_\varphi}+ \sqrt{\mu_\varphi\vphantom{L_\varphi}}}(z_{k+1}^i - z_k^i) \end{align} \end{subequations} where $W_{ij} = [\bar W]_{ij} \otimes I_n$ and $x^{*}_j(w_k)$ is the components of solution of the dual subproblem shared by agent $j$.
nodes.statement_short: Each agent does a gradient step using neighbours' $x_j^*$ and a momentum step.

nodes.name: Construct regularized dual
nodes.statement: Initially, lets construct a regularized dual problem. Then, we have that \begin{align} \min_y \varphi^{\hat\mu}(y) & = \varphi(y) + \frac{\hat\mu}{2}\|y\|_2^2 \end{align} where $\hat\mu = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Regularize the dual with $\hat\mu=\varepsilon/R^2$.

nodes.name: Transfer accuracy to the unregularized dual
nodes.statement: Assume there exists $y_N$ such that \begin{align*} \varphi^{\hat\mu}(y_N) - \varphi^{\hat\mu}_* &\leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2} \end{align*} where $\varphi^{\hat\mu}_*$ is the optimal value of the regularized dual function. Then \begin{align*} \varphi(y_N) - \varphi^* &\leq \varepsilon. \end{align*} where $\varphi^*$ is the optimal value of the dual function.
nodes.statement_short: An $\varepsilon/2$ solution of the regularized dual is $\varepsilon$-optimal for $\varphi$.

nodes.name: Apply known FGM complexity
nodes.statement: It follows from \cite{gas16b} that the number of oracle calls required to find a $(\varepsilon,\tilde{\varepsilon})$-optimal solution is \begin{align*} O\left( \sqrt{\frac{2L_\varphi(\varepsilon + 2R \tilde{\varepsilon})}{\tilde{\varepsilon}^2}}\log\left(\frac{4L_\varphi \left( \min\limits_{Ax=0}F(x)-\min\limits_x F(x))(\varepsilon+2R\tilde{\varepsilon}\right) }{\varepsilon\cdot \tilde{\varepsilon}^2}\right)\right) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Cite the oracle complexity for an $(\varepsilon,\tilde\varepsilon)$-optimal solution.

nodes.name: Bound $R^2$
nodes.statement: Additionally, from Theorem $3$ in \cite{lan17} it follows that \begin{align} R^2 & = \|y^*\|_2^2 \leq \frac{\|\nabla F(x^*)\|_2^2}{\sigma_{\min}(A)} = \frac{M^2}{\sigma_{\min}(A)}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $R^2\le M^2/\sigma_{\min}(A)$ by a cited theorem.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The final results follow by the definitions of $\tilde\varepsilon$ and $L_\varphi$.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute definitions of $\tilde\varepsilon$ and $L_\varphi$.

nodes.name: Regularize the primal
nodes.statement: We can regularize the primal problem in Eq. \eqref{main2} such that we instead try to solve \begin{align*} \min_{Ax=0} F(x) + \frac{\mu}{2}\|x -x^*(z_0)\|_2^2, \end{align*} with $\mu = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2_x}$.
nodes.statement_short: Add $\frac{\mu}{2}\|x-x^*(z_0)\|^2$ with $\mu=\varepsilon/R_x^2$.

nodes.name: Choose the minimizer
nodes.statement: Additionally, if the minimizer $x^*$ is not unique we will consider it as the closest solution from $x^*(z_0)$, i.e. closest to the initial point of the algorithm.
nodes.statement_short: Take the minimizer closest to the starting point.

nodes.name: Reduce to Case 1
nodes.statement: This take us back to the case of \cref{sec:strong_smooth} for which we can conclude that up to logarithmic factor that the number of iterations required is: \begin{align} \tilde{O}\left( \sqrt{\frac{L R_x^2}{\varepsilon}\chi(A^TA)}\right). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the strongly convex smooth case to get the iteration bound.

nodes.name: Regularize primal and dual
nodes.statement: Similarly as in the cases above we will use regularization. We will regularize the primal problem with $\mu = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2_x}$ and then regularize the dual problem too with $\hat{\mu} = \frac{\varepsilon}{R^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Regularize primal with $\varepsilon/R_x^2$ and dual with $\varepsilon/R^2$.

nodes.name: Bound stopping time of Algorithm 2
nodes.statement: Therefore, up to logarithmic factors the \cref{alg:nesterov2} will stop in no more than \begin{align} O\left( \sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)R^2_x(\varepsilon+2R\tilde{\varepsilon})}{\varepsilon\tilde\varepsilon^2}}\right) \end{align} iterations.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the number of iterations of Algorithm 2.

nodes.name: Optimality of the estimate
nodes.statement: Where the estimate in Eq. \eqref{result2_convex} is unimporvable up to logarithmic factors.
nodes.statement_short: The bound is unimprovable up to logs.
